title: Security Trading Policy
date_next_review: At least every 3 years (last revised date shown as 18 November 2024)

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Mirvac Group. Subject to all of the section 6 prohibitions, the Trading Window and written approval regime, notification of any approved Dealing to the Group Company Secretary within 2 business days, and an ASX Appendix 3Y lodged within 5 business days.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of the Mirvac Group and contractors required to comply with Mirvac Group's policies and procedures. Subject to the same section 6 prohibitions and to the Trading Window and written approval regime, with approval from any two members of the Executive Leadership Team, one of whom must be the Group CEO and Managing Director or the Chief Financial Officer.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-executive directors of Mirvac Limited, Mirvac Funds Limited or any other Mirvac Group entity, other than the Chair of a listed entity. Approval comes from the Chair of the Board of Mirvac Limited and Mirvac Funds Limited with the support of the Group CEO and Managing Director.

tiers.name: Chair of Mirvac Limited, Mirvac Funds Limited or any other listed entity within the Mirvac Group
tiers.description: The Chair of a listed Mirvac entity, who cannot self-clear: approval comes from the Chair of the Mirvac Group Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee with the support of the Group CEO and Managing Director.

tiers.name: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director
tiers.description: The Group CEO and Managing Director. Approval requires both the Chair of the Board of Mirvac Limited and Mirvac Funds Limited and the Chair of the Mirvac Group Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee, with the support of the Chief Financial Officer.

tiers.name: Executive Leadership Team
tiers.description: Members of the Executive Leadership Team other than the Group CEO and Managing Director and the Chief Financial Officer. Approval comes from the Group CEO and Managing Director (or their delegate, the CFO) and the Mirvac Group Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee Chair (or their delegate).

tiers.name: Chief Financial Officer
tiers.description: The Chief Financial Officer. Approval comes from the Group CEO and Managing Director and the Mirvac Group Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee Chair (or their delegate).

tiers.name: consultants and contractors of the Mirvac Group whose terms of engagement apply this policy to them
tiers.description: Consultants and contractors whose engagement terms apply the policy; treated as Employees for the purposes of the prohibitions and the approval regime.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: A Director's or Employee's spouse, de facto or partner; dependent children and other dependants; any trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement under which they or their family may be a beneficiary; any company they or their family control or majority own; any other entity in which they are a director, secretary or executive officer; and any investment manager acting for them or their Associates. An Associate must not Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities without approval obtained under the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in financial products or other arrangements to hedge the value of either: (i) unvested awards; or (ii) vested awards that remain subject to a holding lock granted under any employee security scheme

windows.start_anchor: the next business day after the day on which the half-year or full year results are released (as applicable to the relevant entity)
windows.end_anchor: 6 weeks later, unless varied or cancelled under section 5

windows.start_anchor: the next business day after the day of the Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: 2 weeks later, unless varied or cancelled under section 5

windows.start_anchor: commencement of any period advised by the Mirvac Group to be a Trading Window (notified by the Group Company Secretary by email)
windows.end_anchor: closure of that period as notified by the Group Company Secretary

windows.start_anchor: any time outside a Trading Window (the policy is closed by default: Dealing is only permitted in a Trading Window with written consent, outside a window where Special Circumstances exist, or as an Excluded Dealing)
windows.end_anchor: commencement of the next Trading Window

windows.start_anchor: declaration of a trading blackout by the Mirvac Group at its discretion and without prior notice
windows.end_anchor: as varied or cancelled by the Mirvac Group

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Mirvac Group may at any time declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts, or vary or cancel any existing trading window or trading blackout, at its discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary; the Group Company Secretary notifies Directors and Employees by email when a Trading Window commences and closes. Separately, no reason is given for the grant or refusal of approval to Deal, the Approving Officers may take into account future matters, plans and intentions of the Mirvac Group, and the person must keep confidential whether their request was approved.

rules.detail: A blanket, unqualified ban on derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities. It is not limited by security state, by venue, by direction or by whether the underlying securities are plan securities, and no Approving Officer has power to waive it. Both legs of an OTC collar are derivative agreements in respect of Relevant Mirvac Securities and are therefore prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may enter into any: ... (c) derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities.

rules.detail: Transactions in financial products or other arrangements to hedge the value of unvested awards are prohibited, as are derivative agreements in respect of any unvested Securities, performance rights, options or other awards under any employee security scheme.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may enter into any: (a) transactions in financial products or other arrangements to hedge the value of either: (i) unvested awards ... (b) derivative agreements in respect of any unvested Securities, performance rights, options or other awards pursuant to any employee security scheme

rules.detail: The hedging ban expressly extends to vested awards that remain subject to a holding lock granted under any employee security scheme, so shares released from performance conditions but still inside a disposal restriction cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: vested awards that remain subject to a holding lock granted under any employee security scheme

rules.detail: Although the hedging limb in 6.2(a) is confined to unvested and holding-locked awards, the separate prohibition in 6.2(c) on derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities catches any derivative hedge over fully vested, unrestricted securities as well. There is no clearance route and no vesting-based carve-out.
rules.evidence: derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward, equity swap or collar-plus-loan structure is a derivative agreement in respect of Relevant Mirvac Securities under 6.2(c) and, where the securities are pledged, a loan or other financial arrangement granting security rights to a third party under 6.3. Both are absolute prohibitions.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may enter into, or maintain, any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party.

rules.detail: Outright and permanent ban on short selling Relevant Mirvac Securities, with no definition of short selling, no clearance route and no exception for Trading Windows.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may engage in short selling of Relevant Mirvac Securities at any time.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and is not listed among the section 6 prohibitions. A stock loan involves disposing of Relevant Mirvac Securities and entering into an obligation to reacquire them, both of which fall within the definition of Dealing, so it could only be done inside a Trading Window with the written consent of the Approving Officers; in practice the associated collateral arrangements would engage the 6.3 ban.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes: (a) applying for, acquiring or disposing of, Securities or entering into an agreement to do so; and (b) arranging, granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of Securities

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are derivative agreements in respect of Relevant Mirvac Securities and so caught by 6.2(c); a short CFD would additionally be short selling under 6.4 and, being typically closed within six months, speculative Dealing under 6.1.
rules.evidence: derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities

rules.detail: Margin loans are named in the heading of 6.3 and caught by its operative words. The prohibition covers entering into and maintaining any such arrangement, so a pre-existing margin loan must be unwound rather than merely not renewed.
rules.evidence: 6.3 Margin loans or other security arrangements. No Director or Employee may enter into, or maintain, any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party.

rules.detail: Granting security rights over Relevant Mirvac Securities to a third party is prohibited whenever it is done under a loan or other financial arrangement. There is no threshold, no approval route and no distinction by security state; an encumbrance wholly unconnected with a loan or financial arrangement is not expressly addressed.
rules.evidence: any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party

rules.detail: A blanket ban on any secured financing over Relevant Mirvac Securities, not limited to margin lending, covering the loan leg of a funded collar. It binds Directors, Employees and (through the Appendix A extension) their Associates, and there is no exemption authority: the Approving Officers' discretion runs only to Trading Window timing and Special Circumstances, not to the section 6 prohibitions.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may enter into, or maintain, any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party.

rules.detail: Speculative Dealing on considerations of a short-term nature is prohibited, short term being defined as a period of six months or less. The prohibition expressly extends to options and derivatives over Relevant Mirvac Securities, which is a longer period than the three months used by most ASX policies.
rules.evidence: No Director or Employee may Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities or options or derivatives over Relevant Mirvac Securities on considerations of a short-term nature (being a period of 6 months or less).

short_term.basis: considerations of a short-term nature, being a period of 6 months or less

exceptions.evidence: An Excluded Dealing ... means Dealing in the Relevant Mirvac Securities: (a) that results in no change in beneficial interest in the Relevant Mirvac Securities;
where the Dealing occurs via investments in a scheme or other arrangement where the investment decisions are exercised by a third party;
where the Director or Employee has no control or influence with respect to Dealing decisions;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer in relation to Relevant Mirvac Securities;

an acquisition of Securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend or distribution plan where the Director or Employee did not enter into or amend their participation in the plan outside a Trading Window.

an application for performance rights under any employee security scheme or an allotment of Securities pursuant to any employee security scheme ... (for the avoidance of doubt, the subsequent disposal of Relevant Mirvac Securities acquired under an employee security scheme is subject to the prohibitions outlined in this policy)

exceptions.approver: Approving Officers (written consent obtained on a confidential basis, under section 5)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship for a pressing financial commitment which cannot be satisfied other than by disposing of Relevant Mirvac Securities;
to comply with the requirements of a court order or other legal or regulatory requirement;
any other circumstance which is considered to be an exceptional circumstance by the Approving Officers.

exemption_authority: The Approving Officers may consent in writing, on a confidential basis, to Dealing outside a Trading Window where Special Circumstances exist (court order or other legal or regulatory requirement, severe financial hardship for a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied other than by disposing of Relevant Mirvac Securities, or any other circumstance they consider exceptional). That discretion goes only to timing: nothing in the policy allows any Approving Officer or the Board to waive the section 6 prohibitions on derivatives, hedging, secured financing, short selling or speculative Dealing. Approvals may not be retrospective and no reason is given for a grant or refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Director or Employee may enter into any ... derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single limb defeats a collar on its own: it is not confined to unvested or plan securities, not confined to exchange-traded products, and carries no clearance route, so both the purchased put and the written call are prohibited even over fully vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: enter into or maintain secured financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: No Director or Employee may enter into, or maintain, any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Mirvac Relevant Securities are granted to a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is separately and absolutely prohibited, and the word 'maintain' means an arrangement entered into before appointment or before the policy must be unwound rather than simply run off.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Special Circumstances and the Approving Officers' consent operate only as exceptions to the Trading Window requirement in section 2; section 6 contains no equivalent discretion.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no person or committee who can approve the structure, so a funded collar cannot be rescued by disclosure, board approval or hardship, only by a change to the policy itself.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing includes ... arranging, granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even setting aside 6.2(c), writing the call and later exercising or discharging either leg are each separate Dealings requiring their own approval inside a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.topic: five business day approval and automatic lapse
bespoke_clauses.clause: An approval must ... not be for a period of more than 5 business days ... An approval lapses immediately and without further notification if a Director or Employee to whom an approval has been given acquires Inside Information or if a Trading Window closes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted transaction must be instructed within five business days and dies instantly if the window closes or inside information arises, which is unworkable for a multi-leg structure requiring simultaneous pricing and documentation.

bespoke_clauses.topic: settlement may fall outside the window
bespoke_clauses.clause: once the instruction to trade has been placed, the Dealing may settle outside of the Trading Window or approval period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only timing relief in the policy: settlement mechanics can run past a window provided the instruction was given inside it, which would matter for a physically settled structure if the substantive prohibitions did not already apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In considering whether to approve, the Approving Officers may take into account future matters, plans and intentions of the Mirvac Group. ... No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of approval to Deal. A Director or Employee must keep confidential whether their request to Deal is approved or not approved.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why an approval was refused or even that it was sought, so execution risk on any permitted dealing cannot be diligenced from the company side.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy places a restriction on a Director or Employee in Dealing in Relevant Mirvac Securities, the Director or Employee must not knowingly allow a Dealing in Relevant Mirvac Securities by any of its Associates. ... An Associate of the Director or Employee must not Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities without approval being obtained in accordance with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a family trust, controlled company, an entity where the executive is an officer, or an investment manager does not avoid any of the section 6 prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Director or Employee may Deal in Relevant Mirvac Securities or options or derivatives over Relevant Mirvac Securities on considerations of a short-term nature (being a period of 6 months or less).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The short-term test is six months rather than the usual three and expressly names options and derivatives, so even a permitted option strategy would need a tenor well beyond six months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Mirvac Group may, at any time, declare additional trading windows or trading blackouts, or vary or cancel any existing trading windows or trading blackouts in Relevant Mirvac Securities at any time at its discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Windows can be cancelled without notice, voiding any outstanding Notice of Intention to Deal, so no execution date can be relied on in advance.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy, and is blocked twice over. Section 6.2(c) prohibits Directors and Employees from entering into any derivative agreements in respect of any Relevant Mirvac Securities, without limitation by vesting state, venue or purpose, which defeats both the purchased put and the written call even over fully vested, unrestricted stapled securities; 6.2(a) separately bans hedging unvested awards and vested awards still subject to a holding lock. Section 6.3 then prohibits entering into or maintaining any loan or other financial arrangement under which security rights over Relevant Mirvac Securities are granted to a third party, which is the loan leg, and the word 'maintain' means any pre-existing facility must be unwound. There is no exemption authority capable of curing this: the Approving Officers' written consent and the Special Circumstances gateway relate only to dealing outside a Trading Window, not to the section 6 prohibitions, and approvals cannot be retrospective, last at most five business days and lapse automatically when a window closes. Short selling is banned at any time and speculative dealing in options or derivatives on a horizon of six months or less is also prohibited, so no variant of the structure survives without a change to the policy itself.
